paragraphs.source_en: “There is one matter Ieyasu has never been able to put from his mind: your honored father’s last wish. When Fushimi Castle was besieged by the Jibu and your father died there, he left behind one fervent wish. The Jibu knew your father well, and that is why he spoke as he did. So be it. I leave the Jibu in your hands.”

units.source_en: “There is one matter Ieyasu has never been able to put from his mind: your honored father’s last wish.

ja.t: れぬことがある。それは、そなたの

units.source_zh: “家康有件心事一直放不下，便是令尊的心愿。

units.source_en: When Fushimi Castle was besieged by the Jibu and your father died there, he left behind one fervent wish.

ja.t: っていたことがあった。

paragraphs.source_zh: “家康有件心事一直放不下，便是令尊的心愿。当初伏见城被治部包围，令尊殉难时有个执著的愿望。治部也深知令尊，才会如此说。既这样，治部就交给你了。”

paragraphs.source_en: At these words, Mitsunari’s vision went black and the world spun around him. He had assumed that he would be sent to Osaka. Moreover, it was his old friend Tanaka Yoshimasa who had gone to hunt him down, and that too had afforded him a measure of comfort.

units.source_en: At these words, Mitsunari’s vision went black and the world spun around him.
units.source_zh: 一听此话，三成只觉眼前发黑，天旋地转。

units.source_en: He had assumed that he would be sent to Osaka.
units.source_zh: 他原以为，自己会被送到大坂。

units.source_en: Moreover, it was his old friend Tanaka Yoshimasa who had gone to hunt him down, and that too had afforded him a measure of comfort.
units.source_zh: 并且，前去搜捕他的乃是旧友田中吉政，这无形中也给了他一丝安慰。

paragraphs.source_zh: 一听此话，三成只觉眼前发黑，天旋地转。他原以为，自己会被送到大坂。并且，前去搜捕他的乃是旧友田中吉政，这无形中也给了他一丝安慰。

paragraphs.source_en: Mitsunari had grown accustomed to Yoshimasa’s courteous treatment, and that was why he had carelessly misspoken before Ieyasu. In former days he had spoken his mind bluntly to anyone, without the least courtesy; but today, so long as no one taunted him, he had meant not to provoke anyone—only to let slip, in a careless moment, a meaningless outburst of spite.

units.source_en: Mitsunari had grown accustomed to Yoshimasa’s courteous treatment, and that was why he had carelessly misspoken before Ieyasu.
units.source_zh: 三成已经习惯了吉政的礼遇，才在家康面前一不留神说错了话。

units.source_en: In former days he had spoken his mind bluntly to anyone, without the least courtesy; but today, so long as no one taunted him, he had meant not to provoke anyone—only to let slip, in a careless moment, a meaningless outburst of spite.

ja.t: らせるつもりはなかった。それなのに、ふとした

units.source_zh: 若是从前，无论在谁面前，他也直言不讳，毫不客气，可今日，只要别人不冷嘲热讽，他也没打算主动惹恼对方，可一不留神，竟然说了句毫无意义的气话。

paragraphs.source_zh: 三成已经习惯了吉政的礼遇，才在家康面前一不留神说错了话。若是从前，无论在谁面前，他也直言不讳，毫不客气，可今日，只要别人不冷嘲热讽，他也没打算主动惹恼对方，可一不留神，竟然说了句毫无意义的气话。

paragraphs.source_en: In truth, it had been an outrageous lie. If he found fault with his sentence, Mitsunari was resolved to protest it loudly. Yet what he had said was, “Do with me as you please.” With that single remark, Mitsunari gave Ieyasu the opening he needed to place his life and fate, without a moment’s hesitation, in the hands of the orphaned son of Torii Mototada.

units.source_en: In truth, it had been an outrageous lie.
units.source_zh: 其实，这是天大的谎话。

units.source_en: If he found fault with his sentence, Mitsunari was resolved to protest it loudly.
units.source_zh: 若是对处置心存不满，三成必会大声辩驳，这是他的决心。

units.source_en: Yet what he had said was, “Do with me as you please.”
units.source_zh: 可他偏偏说了“悉听尊便”。

units.source_en: With that single remark, Mitsunari gave Ieyasu the opening he needed to place his life and fate, without a moment’s hesitation, in the hands of the orphaned son of Torii Mototada.
units.source_zh: 就这一句话，让家康顺水推舟，毫不迟疑把三成的身家性命交给了鸟居元忠的遗孤。

paragraphs.source_zh: 其实，这是天大的谎话。若是对处置心存不满，三成必会大声辩驳，这是他的决心。可他偏偏说了“悉听尊便”。就这一句话，让家康顺水推舟，毫不迟疑把三成的身家性命交给了鸟居元忠的遗孤。

paragraphs.source_en: “You must be very weary. Go and rest at Torii Kyūgorō’s camp.”

units.source_en: “You must be very weary. Go and rest at Torii Kyūgorō’s camp.”
units.source_zh: “想必您也很是疲劳，快到鸟居久五郎营中去歇息吧。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “想必您也很是疲劳，快到鸟居久五郎营中去歇息吧。”

paragraphs.source_en: Urged on by Honda Masazumi, Mitsunari rose, utterly taken aback by the outcome. Ishida Mitsunari, who had contended with Ieyasu for mastery of the realm, had meant to die with dignity; never had he imagined that one angry remark would leave him helpless prey upon Torii Kyūgorō’s chopping block.

units.source_en: Urged on by Honda Masazumi, Mitsunari rose, utterly taken aback by the outcome.
units.source_zh: 在本多正纯的催促下，三成站了起来，事情的结果让他大感意外。

units.source_en: Ishida Mitsunari, who had contended with Ieyasu for mastery of the realm, had meant to die with dignity; never had he imagined that one angry remark would leave him helpless prey upon Torii Kyūgorō’s chopping block.

ja.t: ぬつもりでいた。それが、たった

units.source_zh: 与家康争夺天下的石田三成，本打算堂堂正正死去，没想到因为一句气话，竟沦落为鸟居久五郎俎上鱼肉。

paragraphs.source_zh: 在本多正纯的催促下，三成站了起来，事情的结果让他大感意外。与家康争夺天下的石田三成，本打算堂堂正正死去，没想到因为一句气话，竟沦落为鸟居久五郎俎上鱼肉。

paragraphs.source_en: Death was death, but how one died made all the difference. One way was to die valiantly for the Toyotomi clan as commander-in-chief of the Western Army, leaving an honored name to posterity; the other was to be killed like a dog so that Torii Naritsugu might avenge his father. To Mitsunari, the gulf between those two deaths was as vast as that between heaven and earth.

units.source_en: Death was death, but how one died made all the difference.
units.source_zh: 横竖都是死，但怎样死，意味却大不一样。

units.source_en: One way was to die valiantly for the Toyotomi clan as commander-in-chief of the Western Army, leaving an honored name to posterity;
units.source_zh: 一是作为西军总大将，为了丰臣氏英勇就死，流芳百世；

units.source_en: the other was to be killed like a dog so that Torii Naritsugu might avenge his father.
units.source_zh: 一是为鸟居成次报父仇所杀，如一只狗。

units.source_en: To Mitsunari, the gulf between those two deaths was as vast as that between heaven and earth.
units.source_zh: 对三成来说，两种死法有如天壤之别。

paragraphs.source_zh: 横竖都是死，但怎样死，意味却大不一样。一是作为西军总大将，为了丰臣氏英勇就死，流芳百世；一是为鸟居成次报父仇所杀，如一只狗。对三成来说，两种死法有如天壤之别。

paragraphs.source_en: Mitsunari, this is the very image of your life. To ruin a lifetime’s illustrious name with a single angry remark—this is the doom from which you have never been able to escape! Mitsunari understood at last, but it was too late. Torii Kyūgorō Naritsugu was still young; faced with his father’s killer, he would surely mock him every way he could before carving him to pieces.

units.source_en: Mitsunari, this is the very image of your life.

ja.t: よ、これこそが、おまえの

units.source_zh: 三成，这其实是你一生的真实写照啊。

units.source_en: To ruin a lifetime’s illustrious name with a single angry remark—this is the doom from which you have never been able to escape!
units.source_zh: 仅仅由于一句气话，就让一生英名毁于一旦，这是你终生摆脱不掉的劫数！

units.source_en: Mitsunari understood at last, but it was too late.
units.source_zh: 三成终于醒悟过来，但为时已晚。

units.source_en: Torii Kyūgorō Naritsugu was still young; faced with his father’s killer, he would surely mock him every way he could before carving him to pieces.
units.source_zh: 鸟居久五郎成次年纪尚轻，面对杀父仇人，他定会百般嘲弄之后，再千刀万剐。

paragraphs.source_en: Honda Masazumi led Mitsunari out. Kyūgorō silently bowed to Ieyasu before following.

units.source_en: Honda Masazumi led Mitsunari out. Kyūgorō silently bowed to Ieyasu before following.
units.source_zh: 本多正纯把三成带出去，久五郎默默向家康施一礼，方才走了出去。

paragraphs.source_en: Once outside Ieyasu’s encampment, Mitsunari was handed over to Torii’s retainers.

units.source_en: Once outside Ieyasu’s encampment, Mitsunari was handed over to Torii’s retainers.

paragraphs.source_en: Torii Naritsugu’s quarters were indeed not far away. Adjoining Honda Tadakatsu’s camp, they occupied the requisitioned residence of a wealthy merchant, built with its back to the lake.

units.source_en: Torii Naritsugu’s quarters were indeed not far away. Adjoining Honda Tadakatsu’s camp, they occupied the requisitioned residence of a wealthy merchant, built with its back to the lake.

paragraphs.source_en: After Mitsunari arrived, Naritsugu sternly ordered his men to tighten security, then led him to an inner room. It stood beside Naritsugu’s own room and appeared to serve as a guest chamber.

units.source_en: After Mitsunari arrived, Naritsugu sternly ordered his men to tighten security, then led him to an inner room.

Ieyasu had placed him in Torii Naritsugu’s hands so the Torii brothers might avenge their father, yet Naritsugu was telling him to rest well. It was exceedingly strange. To think that one of Ieyasu’s close retainers could be so peculiar.

units.source_en: To think that one of Ieyasu’s close retainers could be so peculiar.

paragraphs.source_en: Yet this man before him, ignorant of worldly ways and awkwardly taciturn, would be transformed upon the battlefield into a lion capable of facing a host of thousands. Perhaps therein lay the singular genius of Tokugawa Ieyasu, who had gathered all the warriors of Mikawa beneath his banner. If Torii Naritsugu’s words and manner were this strange, the revenge he devised must surely be strange as well.

paragraphs.source_en: As Mitsunari pondered this, an unusual sound suddenly came from the lakeshore. He quietly opened the window a crack and peered outside. A crowd of men was busily at work. With grim faces, they formed a line and carried bundles of bamboo and timber into the pine grove. Plainly they were erecting a palisade—perhaps even preparing an execution ground. Remembering Naritsugu’s furious glare, Mitsunari felt certain he would not be permitted to die calmly by his own hand.
